Since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=\frac{5}{2},$ we will use a step size of 

$$
Δx=\frac{5}{2}-2=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

First, we add the initial condition data:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2$ | ${e}^{2}$ |  |  |

Next, we compute ${y}^{′}$ according to the given rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡y \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2}) \\  & =2\cdot 2 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

So, we add this to our table:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2$ | ${e}^{2}$ | $4$ |  |

Next, we compute $Δy$ using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

We add this to our table:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2$ | ${e}^{2}$ | $4$ | $2$ |

To get the values of $x$ and $y$ in the *next* row, we add $Δx$ to $x$ and $Δy$ to $y,$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx \\  & =2+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{2} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\  & ={e}^{2}+2\end{aligned}
$$

Adding these rows to our table gives the following:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2$ | ${e}^{2}$ | $4$ | $2$ |
| $\frac{5}{2}$ | ${e}^{2}+2$ |  |  |

Therefore, we conclude that $y(\frac{5}{2})≈{e}^{2}+2.$
